Security review of the Filesystem Layout MCP/API surface. Found and closed a HIGH policy bypass (F-1): grant scope.paths governed only the audit target, which on this surface is a layout id (spec 9) and None for register's spec form, so a path-scoped grant was silently ignored - the spec form wrote its store outside the allow-list while the inline form was refused, and no mutation ever had its store_path checked. Fix: policy path subjects are now a gate input (pep::check_with_paths + dispatch path_subjects), separate from the audit target, declared by the four mutations as the store (write) plus spec/fstab when it names a file (read); an out-of-scope subject is refused before any read or write. Also closed F-2 (R-11 missed nested argument text, so an injection payload stored in the inline layout object was persisted and echoed by get - scan now walks nested objects/arrays) and F-3 (is_irreversible did not list the four mutations, so the PEP itself would allow an unauthenticated mutation if a call site forgot require_grant). Hardening of the Filesystem Layout MCP/API surface. Three defects found and fixed on the persistence layer all ten aios.fs_layout.* tools share. H-1 (HIGH): nothing bounded the write side while every read enforces the 10 MiB ceiling, so an accumulating store could be saved successfully past it and was then unreadable forever - reproduced end-to-end through the real MCP binary (register#11 reported ok=True while writing 11,027,499 bytes; #12 onwards failed forever at read with 'exceeds 10 MiB security size limit'). save_to_path now refuses on the serialized bytes before staging anything, so the destination is untouched, the previous store stays readable, and the refusal is explicit. H-2 (MEDIUM): closes the unbounded staged-file retention T-01537 F-5 assigned here - MAX_STAGED_KEEP=8 refuses to stage another preserved .tmp file, checked before staging, prefix-scoped per store so stores sharing one .aios/ directory cannot trip each other's cap, and nothing is ever deleted (a staged file beside a different writer's store is that writer's data). H-4 (MEDIUM): the final atomic replace was single-attempt, so one transient lock (Windows os error 5, reproduced on this host) became a permanent failure plus stranded residue - now a bounded retry (5 attempts, 5 s budget, doubling backoff) for transient-only errors, reporting its attempt count and still naming the preserved file. H-3 (MEDIUM): the partial-write cleanup discarded a failed unlink with 'let _ =', so a truncated file that looks like a store could be left silently - both failures are now reported. Verified: test_fs_layout_service 14 -> 17 tests with all three new tests negative-controlled (reverted to HEAD they fail and the pre-existing 14 stay green; file restored byte-identical by cmp), FL1..FL8 PASS, MCP contract C1..C8 PASS, aiosh-mcp 17/0, aiosh-core 591/0 across 30 test binaries, aiosh-cli 24/0; both new refusals return the standard isError envelope with exactly one outcome=error audit row whose detail carries the reason, and aiosh audit verify stays ok. Read-only paths were verified rather than assumed (no process spawn and no DB connection on this surface), so no timeouts were invented around syscalls that cannot be cancelled. Residuals named with owners, not implied closed: read-tool gating (F-4) and F-2's read side are spec-level decisions (docs/filesystem_layout.md 8.1); DirectorySpec::description remains unbounded, so the write cap is the load-bearing invariant; the audit ring's own concurrency defects (F-02/F-06/F-16) live in dispatch/audit and are out of this surface. bash ci/run_all_smokes.sh cannot run on this host - tools/ci_run.py spawns [bash, ...] and Windows resolves bash to the WSL stub with no distro installed (0/29, aborts at suite 1, pre-existing and independent of this change).
